## Introduction

In this activity, reproduce the summary in your prepared
environment, then change a model setting and predict which targets
will run. Continue with your completed `workspace/_targets.R` and
`workspace/report.qmd`, starting from the full dataset and REML.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Get back on track {#recover-reproduce}

Run this from the project root if you need to rebuild
the starting summary or repeat the exercise after changing the dataset
or estimator. Recovery selects the full 29-study dataset, backs up your
working pipeline in `workspace/`, and runs the reference pipeline with
REML. If you lost your report, copy your saved `report.qmd` back into
`workspace/` or complete the
[Quarto report exercise](06_quarto.qmd) before continuing.

``` r
withr::with_dir(
  here::here(),
  source("pipelines/recover_workshop.R")
)
```
:::

## Step 1: rebuild from your selected input

Compare your current `meta-summary.csv` file with a new rebuild in the same environment and with the same local board by re-running the targets pipeline. 

The `identical()` function will compare the new summary with the old.

```{r health-modify-reproduce, eval = FALSE}
withr::with_dir(
  here::here(),
  source("pipelines/workshop_support.R")
)
workshop_dir <- workshop_output_dir()
pipeline_script <- here::here("workspace", "_targets.R")
pipeline_store <- here::here(workshop_dir, "_targets")
summary_path <- here::here(workshop_dir, "meta-summary.csv")
if (!file.exists(pipeline_script) || !file.exists(summary_path)) {
  stop("Run the Get back on track command at the top of this lesson.")
}

before <- read.csv(summary_path)
targets::tar_invalidate(targets::everything(), store = pipeline_store)
targets::tar_make(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)
identical(before, read.csv(summary_path))
```

Expect `TRUE`, meaning that the two `meta-summary.csv` files (the original and new file) are identical. `tar_invalidate()` reruns the analysis and reuses the matching input and model pins. 

## Step 2: make a change and predict the rebuild

In `workspace/_targets.R`, find the `fit` target.
Change `method.tau = "REML"` to `method.tau = "DL"` and save the file.
The alternative estimator is called DerSimonian–Laird.

```{r health-edit-targets-pipeline, eval = FALSE}
file.edit(pipeline_script)
```

We run the targets pipeline, noting that the results of each step are cached. Modifying `fit` will invalidate the cache for that target and its dependencies. But other targets will not be re-run.

```{r health-modify-estimator, eval = FALSE}
targets::tar_outdated(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)
targets::tar_make(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)
after <- read.csv(summary_path)
rbind(
  REML = before[, c("pooled_r", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "tau2")],
  DL = after[, c("pooled_r", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "tau2")]
)
after$pooled_r - before$pooled_r
```

Expect `pipeline_file`, `fit`, `result`, and `summary_file` to be run again.

The input checks and predictive model branch remain up to date. Both pooled estimates round to **0.363**. Switching from REML to DL increases the pooled correlation by about **0.00010** in this dataset. Compare the reported heterogeneity and intervals for the two estimators.

## Step 3: update the report

Run `render_workshop_report()` and reload `workspace/report.html`. The methods section now names the DerSimonian–Laird estimator. 

```{r health-report-render, eval = FALSE}
render_workshop_report()
browseURL(
  here::here("workspace", "report.html")
)
```
